title: Implement scrollable, searchable location dropdowns with cascading behavior

requirements.text: Make the State dropdown fully scrollable with smooth vertical scrolling when the list exceeds screen height. Apply max-height of 60-70% of screen height to the dropdown list container.

quotes: Make the State dropdown fully scrollable when the list exceeds screen height. Use a smooth vertical scroll inside the dropdown/modal.
Add proper max height (for example 60–70% of screen height) to the dropdown list.

acceptanceCriteria: State dropdown scrolls smoothly when state list exceeds available space
Dropdown list has max-height set to 60-70% of viewport height
All states remain selectable without UI overlap

requirements.text: Add search/filter functionality inside the State dropdown for better UX. Users should be able to type to filter the list of states in real-time.

quotes: Enable search/filter inside the State dropdown for better UX.

acceptanceCriteria: Search input field appears at the top of the State dropdown
Typing filters the state list in real-time
Filtered results maintain scrollability

requirements.text: Ensure cascading location selection behavior works correctly: When Country = India, load all Indian states; when State is selected, load districts under that state; when District is selected, load MP constituencies; when MP is selected, load MLA constituencies; then Mandal, then Village.

quotes: Ensure the same cascading behavior: When Country = India → load all Indian states, When State selected → load districts under that state, When District selected → load MP constituencies, When MP selected → load MLA constituencies, Then Mandal → Village

acceptanceCriteria: Selecting India as country loads Indian states
Selecting a state loads districts for that state
Selecting a district loads MP constituencies for that district
Selecting an MP constituency loads MLA constituencies
Selecting MLA constituency loads Mandals
Selecting Mandal loads Villages
Each level clears and resets subsequent dependent levels

requirements.text: Apply the same scroll behavior (smooth vertical scroll, max-height 60-70% of screen, search/filter functionality) to all location dropdowns: State, District, MP, MLA, Mandal, and Village.

quotes: Apply the same scroll behavior to all location dropdowns (State, District, MP, MLA, Mandal, Village).

acceptanceCriteria: All location dropdowns (State, District, MP, MLA, Mandal, Village) have smooth scrolling
All location dropdowns have max-height of 60-70% viewport
All location dropdowns include search/filter functionality
Consistent UX across all dropdown levels

requirements.text: Ensure mobile-responsive and touch-friendly scrolling for all location dropdowns. Fix any z-index or overflow CSS issues that prevent clicks or selections.

quotes: Mobile responsive and touch-friendly scrolling required.
Fix any z-index or overflow issues preventing clicks.

acceptanceCriteria: Dropdowns scroll smoothly on touch devices
No z-index conflicts preventing user interaction
All dropdown items are clickable and selectable
Overflow styles do not clip interactive elements

requirements.text: Optimize dropdown rendering performance to prevent UI freezing when loading and displaying large datasets (hundreds of states, districts, etc.) on Android devices.

quotes: No UI freezing with large datasets

acceptanceCriteria: Dropdown renders large lists without freezing
Scrolling remains smooth with datasets of 100+ items
Search/filter operations are performant on Android

constraints: Must work within React frontend stack (no Flutter; user mentioned Flutter but the existing codebase is React-based)
Use HierarchicalLocationSelector.tsx as the base component for modifications
Must not break existing location selection logic in profile setup and other forms
Backend location data loading logic must remain unchanged unless cascading behavior is broken
nonGoals: Adding new location hierarchy levels beyond the existing six (Country, State, District, MP, MLA, Mandal, Village)
Changing the backend API structure for location data
